meetings.title: Globex: security & roadmap review
segments: Hi Victor, hi Nadia. Can you hear us okay?
Loud and clear. Nadia's joining from the office, I'm at home today.
Hi everyone. Sorry, I'm in a conference room with a very loud air conditioner.
Let me know if it's too much.
You sound fine from here.
Victor, Nadia, thanks for making time.
I know security reviews aren't anyone's favorite meeting.
I brought Daniel, who owns our integrations and identity roadmap, and Noah from solutions engineering.
Thanks Aisha. I'll be direct, because I think that's the most useful thing.
Your product did very well in our evaluation.
My team likes it. The only thing standing between us and procurement is identity and auditability.
That's great to hear. Can I ask what stood out in the evaluation?
It helps us to know what's landing.
Honestly, it was my product team that pushed for it.
They ran a two week trial on our support tickets, and they found a billing issue in the first three days that had been sitting in the queue for a month. That got my attention.
And the setup was easy. That's rare for us.
That's really good to hear.
Walk us through what you need.
Three things. First, SAML single sign-on through Okta, and we need to be able to enforce it.
No local passwords for our employees.
Second, audit logs. Who logged in, who exported data, who changed permissions.
Retained for at least a year.
Third, a committed date for both, in writing.
And ideally SCIM, so accounts are removed automatically when someone leaves.
But that's a nice-to-have, not a blocker.
Nadia, when you say SCIM is a nice-to-have, what's the workaround in the meantime?
A quarterly access review. We export the user list from each tool and check it against HR.
It's manual, but it works, and it's what we do for most vendors today.
We can make that export easy.
There's already a user list export in admin settings, and it includes last login dates.
Last login is actually the most useful field for us. Good.
That's very clear, thank you.
On SAML, we're building it with Okta and Azure AD as the first two providers, with an 'enforce SSO' setting for admins.
On audit logs, the events you listed are exactly the ones in our draft.
SCIM would come after the first release.
How would enforcement work in practice?
If someone at Globex tries to log in with a password, what happens?
Once an admin turns on enforcement, password login is disabled for everyone in the workspace, except one break-glass admin account.
That account is there in case your identity provider has an outage, so you're never locked out of your own data.
Every use of it is logged.
That's the right design. We'll want to know who holds the break-glass account and we'll rotate it ourselves.
Exactly. It's yours to control.
And the date?
Honest answer: we have our quarterly planning session later today, where we're making the final call on sequencing.
I'd rather give you a date that comes out of that than guess now.
I'll come back to you with a written date by end of next week.
That's reasonable. I'd rather wait a week for a real date than get a guess today.
I can work with that.
If I have a date in writing by end of next week, we can start procurement this quarter.
If it slips past that, we're into next fiscal year, and that means a full re-approval.
Could the contract include the SSO date as a commitment? Would that help procurement?
Yes. If the contract says SSO and audit logs will be available by a specific date, with an exit clause if you miss it, procurement is comfortable.
We've done that with other vendors.
That's very workable on our side.
I'll check with our legal team, but I don't expect any issue.
Understood. That's exactly why I don't want to guess.
Can I ask about the audit logs?
We send everything to Splunk.
Is there a native integration, or an API we can pull from?
At launch there'll be a CSV export and an API endpoint for audit logs.
A native Splunk app is on the list, but not in the first release.
Most teams we talk to pull from the API on a schedule.
The API is fine. We do that for a dozen other vendors.
A few other questions from the questionnaire.
Where is our data stored, is it encrypted at rest, and does any of our customer feedback get sent to a third party AI provider?
Before I answer, is there a particular concern behind the AI question?
It helps me be specific.
Mostly that our customers' complaints could end up training someone else's model.
That's the scenario my board asks about.
Data is stored in the US, encrypted at rest and in transit.
For the AI features, feedback text is sent to our model provider for processing, under an agreement that it isn't used for training and isn't retained.
We also redact emails and phone numbers before anything is sent.
How long do you keep the feedback itself?
And can we delete it on request?
You control retention. By default we keep everything while you're a customer.
You can set a retention window, like twenty four months, and anything older is deleted automatically.
And admins can delete specific records or an entire source at any time.
And deletion would show up in the audit log?
Yes. Data deletion is one of the audit log events.
Who did it, when, and what scope.
Good. That covers most of what our privacy team will ask.
Can you put that in a data flow diagram?
My team will want to see exactly where the text goes.
Yes. I'll send you a data flow diagram for the AI features, including what's redacted and where.
When can we expect the diagram?
My team meets on the first of the month to review open vendor items.
Within a few days. Well before your review.
I'll include the redaction steps and the retention policy for the AI provider on the same page.
Good. One page is exactly right.
My team won't read ten.
One more practical thing. Could we get a sandbox workspace, so my team can test the admin settings and the audit log export ourselves once they exist?
Absolutely. I'll set up a sandbox workspace for your team this week and send over the credentials.
Can the sandbox have realistic data?
Testing permissions on an empty workspace doesn't tell us much.
Yes. I'll load it with a sample dataset, a few thousand anonymized support tickets, so the themes and permissions behave like they would in production.
Perfect.
Let me recap. Written SSO and audit log date from me by end of next week.
The data flow diagram from Daniel.
A sandbox from Noah. And we'll update the security questionnaire answers with everything we discussed.
That's right. Thank you, this was a productive conversation.
Better than most vendor security reviews, honestly.
We'll take that. Thanks both, talk soon.
One last thing from my side.
Once you have the date, who else needs to be involved on your side to get to signature?
Procurement and legal. Legal usually takes two weeks for a new vendor.
If your paper is standard, it could be faster.
I'll introduce you to our procurement lead once we have the date.
Perfect. I'll send our standard terms ahead of time so legal can start early.
